questions.q: On which day after a baby boy's birth is Brit Milah traditionally performed?
questions.explain: Brit Milah (circumcision) is carried out on the eighth day after birth, following the command given to Abraham.

questions.q: What is the title of the trained specialist who performs the circumcision?
questions.explain: A mohel is specially trained to carry out circumcision safely and according to Jewish law.

questions.q: What does Brit Milah primarily symbolise in Judaism?
options: The covenant between God and Abraham
The giving of the Torah at Sinai
questions.explain: Circumcision is the physical sign of the covenant God made with Abraham and his descendants.

questions.q: What is the name of the person who has the honour of holding the baby during the Brit Milah?
questions.explain: The sandek holds the baby on his lap during the circumcision, an honoured role often given to a grandfather.

questions.q: When is a baby boy given his Hebrew name?
questions.explain: A baby boy is formally named during the Brit Milah on the eighth day.

questions.q: A baby boy is born but is unwell and the doctor advises against surgery on the eighth day. What should the family do?
options: Postpone the Brit Milah until the baby is healthy
Carry it out anyway on the eighth day
Perform it in the synagogue instead of at home
questions.explain: Preserving health takes priority, so circumcision is delayed until the child is well enough.

questions.q: How are baby girls typically named in Jewish tradition?
options: During a Torah reading in the synagogue
By circumcision on the eighth day
At a ceremony held one year later
questions.explain: Baby girls are usually named in the synagogue when the father is called up to the Torah, often on the first Shabbat after birth.

questions.q: At what age does a Jewish boy become Bar Mitzvah?
questions.explain: A boy becomes Bar Mitzvah at the age of 13.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'Bar Mitzvah' literally mean?
questions.explain: 'Bar Mitzvah' translates as 'son of the commandment', marking responsibility to keep the mitzvot.

questions.q: What is the main religious significance of becoming Bar or Bat Mitzvah?
options: Becoming responsible for keeping the commandments
questions.explain: The ceremony marks reaching the age of religious adulthood, when the young person is personally responsible for observing the mitzvot.

questions.q: What does a boy typically do for the first time as part of his Bar Mitzvah?
options: Read from the Torah in the synagogue
Lead the whole community in prayer alone
questions.explain: The boy is called up (aliyah) to read a portion from the Torah for the first time as an adult member.

questions.q: In Orthodox Judaism, at what age does a girl usually become Bat Mitzvah?
questions.explain: In Orthodox tradition a girl reaches Bat Mitzvah at 12, a year earlier than a boy.

questions.q: A boy who has just become Bar Mitzvah attends weekday morning prayers. What item may he now wear that he could not before?
questions.explain: From Bar Mitzvah a boy may wear tefillin (phylacteries) at weekday morning prayer as an adult member of the community.

questions.q: What is the name of the canopy under which a Jewish wedding takes place?
questions.explain: The chuppah is the canopy that symbolises the couple's new home together.

questions.q: What is the 'ketubah'?
questions.explain: The ketubah is the marriage contract setting out the husband's obligations to his wife.

questions.q: Why does the groom break a glass at the end of the wedding ceremony?
options: To remember the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem
To mark the end of the honeymoon
questions.explain: Breaking the glass recalls the destruction of the Temple, a reminder of sorrow even at times of joy.

questions.q: What does the chuppah symbolise?
options: The new home the couple will build together
questions.explain: Open on all sides, the chuppah represents the couple's future home, welcoming to guests.

questions.q: How many days does the intense period of mourning known as 'shiva' last?
questions.explain: Shiva means 'seven' and refers to the seven days of intense mourning after a burial.

questions.q: What is the name of the prayer recited by mourners that praises God?
questions.explain: The Mourner's Kaddish praises God and is traditionally recited by mourners, though it does not mention death.

questions.q: How soon after death is a Jewish burial traditionally carried out?
options: As soon as possible, usually within a day
questions.explain: Jewish law requires burial as soon as possible, often within 24 hours, out of respect for the dead.

questions.q: A woman's father has just been buried. She returns home and sits on a low stool while friends bring food. Which mourning practice is this?
questions.explain: During shiva mourners remain at home, often sitting on low stools, while the community provides support and food.

questions.q: One year after a parent's death, a family lights a special candle that burns for 24 hours. What is this annual observance called?
questions.explain: Yahrzeit is the yearly anniversary of a death, marked by lighting a memorial candle that burns for a full day.
